cap: Placental lactogen makes the mother insulin resistant so that glucose flows to the fetus. Glucose crosses the placenta but insulin does not, so fetal beta cells multiply and flood the fetus with insulin. That fetal hyperinsulinemia drives macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia once the cord is cut, delayed surfactant, polycythemia and polyhydramnios; malformations come only from high glucose during organogenesis, as in pregestational diabetes.
